Chapter 7: Practicing Relaxation and Mindful Pausing.
Even when you’ve got healthy routines in place, life’s pressures can still pile up, can’t they? It’s easy for tension to sneak in and leave you feeling restless. That’s why the next step is all about bringing intentional relaxation and mindful pausing into your day.
Now, this isn’t about avoiding your responsibilities or checking out. It’s about carving out small islands of calm—moments where you let your mind and body reset, even if it’s just for a minute or two.
Picture your mind like a tightly wound spring. If you never give it a chance to unwind, the pressure just keeps growing. But when you pause, breathe, and relax—no matter how briefly—you let that spring loosen up. Suddenly, there’s more flexibility, more ease.
You might try something as simple as taking a few slow breaths before a meeting. Or maybe you set aside five minutes to stretch and shake out any tension.
Here are a few practical ways to bring relaxation into your routine:
Take slow, deep breaths, really tuning in to the feeling of air moving in and out.
Try progressive muscle relaxation—gently tensing and releasing different muscle groups, from your toes all the way up to your shoulders.
Or just pause for a moment and notice what’s happening around you—the sounds, the sights, or any sensations you feel right now.
The best part? You don’t need any fancy gear or a big chunk of time. These little breaks can fit right into your day, wherever you are.
The more you practice pausing and relaxing, the more natural it becomes. Over time, it turns into your go-to response when stress shows up, helping you handle challenges without feeling overwhelmed.
